Because if you reside within these walls, you do not adapt to the Faith. The Faith adapts to you! Instead of bringing the High Septon to heel, you bent your knee to him?"
Baelor opened his mouth to intervene, but the King silenced him with a raised hand.

"Do you think I have not opposed the Faith for twenty years?" Baelenys roared. "I have! Because I have the power to do so. If we acted solely out of concern for the Faith and the smallfolk, there would be a war every single day! We would be drowning in their petty grievances!"
"Your Grace, the verdict is given," Baelor tried again. "There is no turning back. But to prevent a further scandal—"

"Who the fuck is the Sept?!" Baelenys bellowed, rounding on his brother. "The Sept will bend to you! Are you both mad? The Sept was too terrified to excommunicate Gaelor months ago! Do you think I do not know this? Do you know how many High Septons I have seen come and go? A Septon speaks loudly to the crowd, but when you look him in the eye, he stares at his own boots in fear!"
Baelenys turned back to Jace, pointing a thick, trembling finger at his chest. "You are a grinding stone upon my life. You did this solely because it was Gaelor."
Jace opened his mouth to retort, but the King shouted him down.
"Gaelor will likely be King! As his brother, it is your duty to elevate him, to lift him high!" Baelenys paused, his chest heaving. "Why in the Seven Hells did I give you that pin?!"
The insult stung. Jace looked down at the floor, gathering his thoughts, before raising his head. His voice was cold, razor-sharp.

"Elevate him?" Jace asked, stepping forward. "Who are we elevating, Father? A man known to the realm as the Housebreaker? A man who has stained our legacy for centuries to come? For moons, I have taken on every burden of the Red Keep. I have done everything in my power to keep this realm functioning. And as in this trial, I have always strived to be just. Does this man you call a potential king have the cloth of a ruler? Can you truly defend him? Do you have any idea the messes I clean up behind him? In a trial between a man emphasizing his devotion to the Crown and the gods, and a brute who played catch with a little girl's severed head... was I supposed to elevate the brute?"

Jace met his father's furious gaze without blinking. "Despite everything, I tried to deliver the verdict that would best serve our house in the long run. If that verdict required burying that brute in the dirt, then I did it, and I will do it again. Know this. If you do not accept it, you can take this brooch from my chest whenever you please. But know that I recognize no king made of him."
Baelenys turned to Baelor, his face a mask of terrifying calm. "What is he blabbering about? Faith, justice, some other nonsense?"
Baelor remained completely silent.
Baelenys turned slowly back to Jace. "All this idea of being just... we are the ones who define it. What is just and what is not is determined by two words leaving my mouth."
The King stepped closer. "You will never put your brother in the wrong. And he will never do it to you."

Baelenys's hands were shaking. "The badge on your chest is not a toy you can take off and put on as you please! There is no 'take it back whenever you want'! When you wear that badge, there is only one requirement: when I say come, you come. When I say go, you go. When I say make this ruling, you make it! Everything you are already supposed to do as my son!"
Baelor cleared his throat nervously. "Your Grace, perhaps we should rest."

Baelenys ignored him, stepping so close to Jace he could smell the stale wine on the King's breath. "Now that there is a trial by combat... if this Costayne, this knight, whoever the fuck he is, harms your brother, what will you do? And if he kills him? You sentenced the man to the Wall. If he wins, you will have made him a chosen champion in the eyes of the gods."
"If this man actually manages to kill Gaelor," Jace spat, "he will have done the Crown a favor!"
Baelenys froze.
He looked at Baelor. "This... this fucking..."

Without looking back at Jace, Baelenys’s massive hand shot out. He grabbed Jace by the collar of his doublet, hauling him forward, and slammed his hand around Jace's throat. With a terrifying surge of old-man strength, the King drove Jace downward, slamming the side of his son’s face brutally against the heavy oak table.
Baelor lunged forward to intervene, but Baelenys shoved him away with his free hand.

"Do you realize who you are talking about?!" Baelenys roared, spittle flying from his lips as he held Jace pinned to the wood. "He is your brother! There is only one rule! One of you will be King, and the other will protect him, clean up his messes, no matter what! And you are that man! When I name this boy heir, who else is he going to trust? Who else will he lean his back against?!"
Jace, his swollen eye pressed painfully against the oak, gasped for air. "Why does it have to be him?!"
Baelenys hesitated. His grip loosened. He let go of Jace’s neck and stepped back.
As Jace slowly straightened up, gasping, Baelenys brought his fist down onto the table with the force of a falling anvil. The thick oak cracked down the center.
The King turned his back, walking toward the balcony.
Baelor quickly checked Jace, his eyes asking a silent question. Jace waved him off.
"I will pretend I did not hear that," Baelenys said, his voice eerily quiet. "Get out."

"Do not fear, Father," Jace said, adjusting his collar. "I have no eye for the Iron Throne. But if you can name someone other than your eldest child as heir, why name this talentless heap of muscle? Do not worry, I am as loyal to this family as you are. You said it yourself. You said I am the one who resembles you the most. That is exactly why it is our duty to keep this brute away from the throne. What do you see in him? That he obeys you well? You kept the peace for twenty years. We will not survive two years under that man, and I know you realize it. Think on it."
Baelenys did not turn around. He spoke to Baelor. "Get him out of here, before I kill him."

Jace turned and left the solar. Through the corridor windows, he caught a glimpse of Alester and Saera walking in the gardens below. Wiping a trickle of blood from his split lip, Jace went to find his mother.
Deep in the bowels of Flea Bottom, Gaelor had been drinking for hours.
Ser Saathos Maris sat across from him, his broken arm still bound tightly in a sling. The tavern was loud and foul-smelling, a perfect place for princes to hide in plain sight.

"It is beyond belief, my Prince," Saathos muttered, taking a careful sip of ale. "There is no way out of this for you, it seems. The Prince has made you his target. I wish to help you, but I cannot think of what to say without overstepping my bounds."
"That man will do everything in his power to bring me down," Gaelor said, staring into his cup.
"Do you believe he will refuse to recognize you as heir?"
"Of course I do."

Saathos leaned closer over the sticky table. "If I may be so bold... I believe he will refuse as well. And I believe Prince Jacaelon's primary motivation is to guarantee you never sit the Iron Throne."

Gaelor downed his drink. "When I am King, that man will do whatever it takes to murder me. I fear he will plunge the realm into civil war. I do not want to be remembered as the king who shattered the peace my father built for decades."
"So... do you believe we must take action?" Saathos asked carefully, testing the waters. "Is that what you are saying, or am I misunderstanding?"
Gaelor looked up, his blue eyes cold and calculating.

"Since you have been busy lately, I have heard many things coming and going through the keep," Saathos continued smoothly. "And I believe you are not alone in your thoughts. You should speak with him directly, but I believe Maester Cordin is one of those who does not want to see the current order disrupted. He might be... like us."
Gaelor nodded slowly. "As a prince, my duty is to gather as much power in the realm as possible. When I am King, he will be dealt with if necessary."
They continued to drink. This time, Saathos paid the tab.
As Jace made his way toward Queen Jaery's chambers, a figure stepped out from an alcove.
It was Weylar Rocke, the Hand's spymaster.
"My Prince," Weylar whispered. "We must speak."
"I am rather occupied," Jace said, brushing past him. "What is it?"
"Regarding your recent... encounter in Flea Bottom," Weylar said quickly.
Jace stopped dead. He looked up and down the corridor. "Not here."
They hurried into Jace's private study. Jace locked the door behind them.
"Speak," Jace ordered.

"Maester Cordin and Grand Maester Baelor have men sniffing around Flea Bottom to uncover what happened that night," Weylar reported. "I do not know if they have learned the truth yet. But I expanded the search outside the district. I have been absent for days because I turned the city upside down."

Weylar stepped closer, dropping his voice. "My suspicions were correct, as you might guess. Vahaemon has agents planted in Flea Bottom. The whispers say a blind woman met with several individuals outside the district. We tracked them down and made them talk."
Jace crossed his arms, his swollen eye throbbing.
"Visenya came here looking for something," Weylar revealed. "And they believe it is a dragon. She is here to tame a dragon."
Jace’s mind raced. Visenya had been scouring the lost texts in Essos and Volantis. If she had crossed the Narrow Sea, she knew something they did not.

"As you know, dragons are still migrating back from the south," Weylar continued. "She must have believed a dragon, known only through rumor, could be found nearby. But if you ask me... since she revealed herself to you, this may not have been a mission ordered by her father. She failed the moment she took off her blindfold. Or so we think."
"Good work, Weylar," Jace said, tossing a heavy pouch of gold onto the desk.
Weylar smiled, catching the gold. "Oh, my Prince, there is no need. We have a different understanding, you and I. If you keep me closer to your side..."
Jace ignored the blatant attempt at climbing the ladder. "What is this dragon? Do we have any extra information? Has anyone seen where Visenya vanished to? Any guesses?"

"We cornered an old man who has lived here for decades," Weylar said, his tone growing serious. "He had no specific knowledge, being Westerosi, but he heard the Essosi whisper a name. They said it was a descendant of the ghost dragon."
The Cannibal. Or something born of its lineage.
"Understood," Jace said. "Is there anything else? What is your next move?"
"Nothing else, my Prince. What more could there be?" Weylar chuckled nervously. "In truth... I think this is a monumental discovery."
"Alright. Did you not get your gold?" Jace asked pointedly.
Weylar offered a tight smile, bowed his head, and slipped out of the room.
synopsisTr: Sör Costayne'in duruşması büyük bir kargaşayla sona ererek kraliyet ailesini parçalar. Kral Baelenys, Kral Eli ile şiddetli bir yüzleşmeye girerken, Prens Gaelor Bit Çukuru'nun gölgelerinde tehlikeli müttefikler arar.
contentTr: Yedinci Ayın Otuzuncu Günü, FS Doksan Dokuz

Büyük Salon sağır edici bir ses fırtınasıyla patladı. Altın pelerinliler Sör Brant Costayne'i sürükleyerek götürürken demir zincirlerin şangırtısı uğultuyu yarıyordu; şövalyenin başı dikti ve dövüşerek yargılanma talebi hala havada ağır bir şekilde asılı duruyordu.

Prens Gaelor davacı çemberinde donup kalmıştı, yüzü öfkeden mora çalmıştı. Sanki kılıcını çekip kalabalığı oracıkta katledecekmiş gibi görünüyordu. Yukarıda, galeride Prenses Maela ve Saera gözleri fal taşı gibi açılmış, şaşkın bakışlar paylaştılar.

Jace ortadaki sandalyeden kalktı, yüzü sakin bir maske gibiydi. Yüce Üstat Baelor ve Yüce Rahip Berholt'a, kürsünün arkasındaki özel bekleme odasına kadar kendisini takip etmelerini işaret etti. Ağır meşe kapılar kapanıp salonun kaosunu boğduğunda, Yüce Rahip uzun, memnun bir nefes verdi.

"Son derece ihtiyatlı bir karar, Prensim, Yüce Üstat," diye mırıldandı Berholt, kırışık yüzüne dingin bir gülümseme yerleşerek. "Tanrıları öfkelendirmeden insanların yasalarına saygı duyan bir karar verdik. İnanç yatıştırıldı."
Baelor kaskatı bir şekilde başını salladı. "Umarım olabilecek en dengeli sonuç buydu, Yüce Kutsiyetiniz."
Prenses Maela kibar bir reverans yaparak içeri süzüldüğünde kapı hafifçe aralandı. "Yüce Rahip'e kaleden çıkana kadar eşlik edeceğim lordlarım," diye teklif etti.
Berholt başını eğdi ve prensesi takip ederek Jace ile Baelor'u sessiz odada yalnız bıraktı. Kapı mandalı tık ettiği an, diplomatik cila Baelor'un yüzünden silinip gitti. Keskin gözlerle Jace'e döndü.
"Babamın yanına gidelim," dedi Jace, kadife ceketindeki tozu silkelerken. "Sonucu özetlemeliyiz."

"Peki bu kararı Kral'a tam olarak nasıl açıklamayı planlıyorsun?" diye hesap sordu Baelor; bağırmıyordu ama ses tonu suçlama damlıyordu. "Az önce ne yaptığının gerçekten farkında mısın? Absürt bir karardı. Yedi Krallık tarihinde görülmemiş bir şey. Kandan gelen bir prense kılıç çeken bir adamı Duvar'a göndermeye kalkıştın."
Baelor özenle kesilmiş sakalını sıvazladı, çenesi sımsıkıydı. "Bu noktada onu affetseydin de olurdu anasını satayım."

Jace irkilmedi. Kraliyet dairelerine çıkan dolambaçlı merdivenlere doğru yürürlerken sesini düz tuttu. "Salonda da söylediğim gibi Amca, iki tarafın da günahlarını tarttığınızda bunun adil bir karar olduğunu biliyorum. Evet, bir prense kılıç kaldırmanın cezası ölümdür. Ama bu prens Gaelor Targaryen. Hane Yıkan. Demir Taht'ın potansiyel varisi. Bu kararı vererek, inançlı avam tabakasını tekrar kendi tarafımıza çekmeyi ve aynı zamanda Gaelor'un vahşetlerinin tamamen cezasız kalmamasını sağlamayı amaçladım."
"Gaelor'u küçük düşürdün," dedi Baelor, her kelimeyi tartarak.
Jace'in dudakları soğuk bir sırıtışla kıvrıldı. "Bu o kadar korkunç bir şey mi?"
"Bu siyaset, Jace," diye tısladı Baelor merdivenlerde durarak. "Senin kardeş kavgaların için bir oyun alanı değil. Stratejik düşünmen gerekiyor."
"Taç'ın gelecekteki istikrarı için çok iyi bir adım attım," diye karşılık verdi Jace.
"Kinle hareket ettin."
Jace'in sırıtışı kayboldu. "Kararımı kişisel husumetlere veya hırslara dayandırmadım Amca. Ama tavsiyen için teşekkür ederim."
Kral'ın güneş odasının ağır kapılarına ulaştılar.

Gaelor onları geçmişti. Veliaht Prens birkaç dakika önce odaya dalmıştı; haberi Kral'a vermek için önden koşan Üstat Cordin de onu yakından takip ediyordu. Kalın meşenin ardından Jace, Gaelor'un bağırışlarını duyabiliyordu.
Güneş odasının içinde, Kral Baelenys balkonda duruyor, taş korkuluklara yaslanıyordu. Gaelor ise Myr halılarının üzerinde kafese kapatılmış bir ayı gibi volta atıyordu.

"Yedi Krallık tarihinin neresinde bir adamın bir prensi iki kez öldürmeye teşebbüs edip de affedildiği görülmüş?!" diye kükredi Gaelor. "Senin o kıymetli oğlun, tüm ayaktakımının önünde bir Targaryen prensini küçük düşürdü! Adımızı çamura buladı!"
"Prensim, lütfen sakin olun," diye yalvardı Cordin, bir kadeh Arbor kırmızısı sunarak. "Küçük kardeşiniz... onun amatörce hatalarını kabul etmelisiniz. O yeni bir El. Öğrenecek ve gelişecek..."
Gaelor kadehe tokat atarak savurdu. Gümüş oda boyunca uçtu ve duvar halılarına kırmızı şarap saçtı.
"Ne yaptığını çok iyi biliyor!" diye tükürdü Gaelor.
Kral Baelenys elini kaldırarak Gaelor'a sesini alçaltmasını işaret etti.
"Beni ölü görene kadar durmayacak!" diye bağırdı Gaelor emri görmezden gelerek. "O piç kurusu dövüşerek yargılanma talep etti! Onunla kendim yüzleşeceğim! Kellesini bir mızrağa geçireceğim!"
Baelenys balkondan döndü, yara izleriyle dolu yüzü inanamaz bir ifadeyle buruştu. "Duvar'a gönderdiğiniz adam dövüşerek yargılanma mı talep etti?"
O anda ağır kapılar inleyerek açıldı. Jace ve Baelor güneş odasına adım attılar. Sör Alester Dayne koridorda nöbet tutuyor, bu gergin atışmayı izliyordu.
Jace ve Gaelor göz göze geldi. Odadaki hava donmuş gibiydi.
Kral Baelenys kalın bir parmağıyla işaret etti. "Buraya gelin. İkiniz de."
Jace bir adım öne çıktı.

Her şey bir bulanıklık içinde oldu. Gaelor ileri atıldı, acımasız, dengesiz bir yumruğu doğrudan Jace'in yüzüne fırlatırken devasa omuzu düştü. Kaynatılmış deriye sarılı parmak eklemleri, mide bulandırıcı bir çatırtıyla Jace'in elmacık kemiğine çarptı.
Jace şiddetle geriye doğru sendeledi, görüşü beyaz bir ışıkla parladı. Şişen gözünü tutarak Alester'a çarptı.
Alester anında tepki verdi, Jace'i belinden yakaladı ve onu korumak için koridora doğru geri itti. Baelor kardeşlerin arasına girerek ellerini havaya kaldırdı.
"Yeter!" diye böğürdü Kral Baelenys; bu, tavandaki tozu bile sarsan bir kükremeydi.
Kral iki adımda odayı geçti, Gaelor'u tuniğinden yakaladı ve balkona doğru sürükledi. Kan beynine sıçrayan Jace, eli hançerine giderek öne doğru atılmaya çalıştı.
Alester Jace'i belinden yakaladı, onu hafifçe yerden kaldırarak geri çekti.
"Çıkarın şu aptalı buradan!" diye kükredi Baelenys Jace'i işaret ederek.
Alester çırpınan Jace'i güneş odasından dışarı sürükledi. Sürüklenirken Baelor, Jace'in omzuna güven verici bir el koydu.
Baelenys öfkesini Gaelor'a çevirdi. "Sen aklını mı kaçırdın lan?!"
Kral volta attı, elini kel kafasında gezdirdi. "Yeter! Nedir bu delilik? Siz ikiniz tanrılar tarafından gönderilmiş bir bela mısınız?"
Baelenys durdu, derin bir nefes aldı ve Baelor'a baktı. "Bana ne olduğunu anlat."
"Her şeyi o başlattı!" diye bağırdı Gaelor.
Baelenys masadaki ağır gümüş sürahiyi kaptığı gibi doğrudan Gaelor'a fırlattı. Kafasını kıl payı sıyırıp taş duvarda parçalandı.
"Siktir git lan buradan!" diye gürledi Kral. "Defol!"
Gaelor babasına dik dik baktı, ardından kapıyı arkasından sertçe çarparak odadan hışımla çıktı.
Baelenys balkon korkuluğuna ağır bir şekilde yaslandı, şehre doğru baktı. "Konuş, Baelor."

"Majesteleri," dedi Baelor dikkatlice, "eğer Prens Gaelor söyleyeceklerini söylediyse, Prens Jacaelon'unkileri de duymalısınız. Ancak şunu söyleyeceğim... bu kararı vermek benim arzum değildi. Yine de, Taç'a en az zararı verecek şekilde alındı. Böyle korkunç bir karar ne kadar düzgün çıkabilirse o kadar düzgün çıktı."
Baelenys Karasu Körfezi'ne doğru baktı. "Ben bunlarla ne yapacağım? Bu ikisiyle şimdi ne konuşabilirim ki?"
"Majesteleri, oğullarınız arasındaki bağ bu noktada onarılamaz derecede koptu. Eğer onları barıştırmaya dair bir umudunuz varsa, artık bundan vazgeçmelisiniz."
Baelenys yumruğuyla taş korkuluğa vurdu. "Bir prensi öldürmeye çalışan bir adam nasıl olur da Duvar'a mahkum edilir?"

"Yüce Rahip başından beri merhametten yanaydı," diye açıkladı Baelor. "Bir bakıma, avamın gözünde bir fikir birliği oluşturulmuş oldu. Aksi takdirde, mesele Taç ve İnanç arasında açık bir çatışmaya dönüşebilirdi."
Baelenys hiçbir şey söylemedi. Kral muhafızına döndü. "Onu geri getirin. Jace'i bana getirin."
Koridorda Saera, Jace'in hızla şişen, mor gözüne nazikçe dokunuyordu.
"O siktiğimin hayvanı bana kuduz bir köpek gibi saldırdı," diye tısladı Jace, sesi adrenalinle titriyordu. "Onu yok edeceğim. Bu daha hiçbir şey. Beklesin, görecek."
"Sesini alçalt," diye fısıldadı Saera muhafızlara bakarak.
Jace, kapılar açılana kadar Gaelor'un adına lanet okumaya devam etti. "Prensim. Kralımız sizi bekliyor," diye duyurdu bir muhafız.
Alester ve Saera salonda kaldılar. Alester ağırlığını değiştirdi, boş koridora bakındı. "Prenses... burada beklememizi mi tercih edersiniz?"
"Evet," dedi Saera.
Alester tereddüt etti, ağır kapılara baktı. "O halde belki de bahçelerde beklemeliyiz."
Saera durdu, kirpiklerinin altından uzun boylu, hırpalanmış şövalyeye baktı. Dudaklarında hafif, bilmiş bir gülümseme belirdi. "Yol gösterin."
Jace güneş odasına geri döndü. Baelor ocağın yanında sessizce duruyordu.
"Baba, izin ver detayları anlatayım," diye söze başladı Jace.
Baelenys yorgun gözlerini ovuşturdu. "Anlat."

"Amcam Baelor'un aşağı yukarı ne düşündüğünü zaten biliyordum," dedi Jace, kelimelerini tartarak. "Ancak Yüce Rahip'i tarttıktan sonra, inançlı avamın sempatisini geri kazanırken nasıl adil bir sonuç çıkarabileceğimizi düşünmeye başladım. İnanç'ı dışlamadan ve üç yargıç arasında aleni bir bölünme yaratmadan bu işten nasıl temiz bir şekilde çıkabilirdik? Evet, ilk ve bariz ceza ölümdü. Ancak Brant Costayne kalabalığa mükemmel oynadı. Mantıklı konuştu. Ve Gaelor'un kendi eylemlerini teraziye koymadan bir karara varamayacağımız anlaşıldı. Amacım, son zamanlarda karşılaştığımız o muazzam tepkiyi hafifletmekti. Halkın zihnine Targaryenlerin adil olduğu, İnanç'a değer verdiğimiz ve sadece bir prense el kalktı diye körü körüne yargı dağıtmadığımız fikrini ekmekti..."

"İnanç mı?!" diye patladı Baelenys, sesi bir kırbaç gibi şaklayarak. "Kardeşin bizzat bu kalede aforoz edilmedi! Neden biliyor musun? Çünkü bu duvarların içinde yaşıyorsan, İnanç'a uyum sağlamazsın. İnanç sana uyum sağlar! Yüce Rahip'e boyun eğdireceğinize, onun önünde diz mi çöktünüz?"
Baelor araya girmek için ağzını açtı ama Kral elini kaldırarak onu susturdu.

"Yirmi yıldır İnanç'a karşı gelmediğimi mi sanıyorsunuz?" diye kükredi Baelenys. "Geldim! Çünkü bunu yapacak gücüm var. Eğer sadece İnanç'ı ve avamı düşünerek hareket etseydik, her Allah'ın günü bir savaş çıkardı! Onların ufak tefek şikayetlerinde boğulurduk!"
"Majesteleri, karar verildi," diye tekrar denedi Baelor. "Artık geri dönüş yok. Ancak daha büyük bir skandalı önlemek için—"

"Sept de kim oluyor lan?!" diye böğürdü Baelenys kardeşine dönerek. "Sept size boyun eğecek! Siz ikiniz delirdiniz mi? Sept aylar önce Gaelor'u aforoz edemeyecek kadar dehşet içindeydi! Bunu bilmediğimi mi sanıyorsunuz? Kaç tane Yüce Rahip'in gelip gittiğini gördüm biliyor musunuz? Bir Rahip kalabalığa yüksek sesle konuşur, ama onun gözünün içine baktığınızda korkudan kendi çizmelerine bakar!"
Baelenys Jace'e döndü, kalın, titreyen bir parmağıyla onun göğsünü işaret etti. "Sen benim ömür törpümsün. Bunu sadece Gaelor olduğu için yaptın."
Jace karşılık vermek için ağzını açtı ama Kral bağırarak onu bastırdı.

"Gaelor muhtemelen Kral olacak! Onun kardeşi olarak senin görevin onu yüceltmek, onu yükseklere taşımaktır!" Baelenys durakladı, göğsü inip kalkıyordu. "Ben sana o rozeti Yedi Cehennem aşkına neden verdim?!"
Hakaret canını yaktı. Jace düşüncelerini toparlayarak yere baktı, ardından başını kaldırdı. Sesi soğuk ve jilet gibi keskindi.

"Onu yüceltmek mi?" diye sordu Jace bir adım öne çıkarak. "Kimi yüceltiyoruz, Baba? Diyarda Hane Yıkan olarak bilinen bir adamı mı? Mirasımızı yüzyıllar boyunca lekelemiş bir adamı mı? Aylardır Kızıl Kale'nin her yükünü üstlendim. Bu diyarın işlemesini sağlamak için elimden gelen her şeyi yaptım. Ve bu duruşmada olduğu gibi, her zaman adil olmaya çabaladım. Potansiyel bir kral dediğin bu adamda bir hükümdar kumaşı var mı? Onu gerçekten savunabilir misin? Onun arkasından hangi pislikleri temizlediğim hakkında hiçbir fikrin var mı? Taç'a ve tanrılara bağlılığını vurgulayan bir adamla, küçük bir kızın kesik başıyla yakalamaca oynayan bir hayvan arasındaki davada... o hayvanı mı yüceltmeliydim?"

Jace babasının öfkeli bakışlarına gözünü kırpmadan karşılık verdi. "Her şeye rağmen, uzun vadede hanemize en çok hizmet edecek kararı vermeye çalıştım. Eğer o karar bu hayvanı çamura gömmeyi gerektiriyorsa, yaptım ve yine yaparım. Şunu bil. Eğer bunu kabul etmiyorsan, bu broşu göğsümden istediğin zaman alabilirsin. Ama bil ki benim onun gibi bir kralım olmayacak."
Baelenys Baelor'a döndü, yüzü dehşet verici bir sakinlik maskesi takınmıştı. "Bu ne zırvalıyor? İnanç, adalet, bilmem ne saçmalığı?"
Baelor tamamen sessiz kaldı.
Baelenys yavaşça Jace'e geri döndü. "Bütün bu adil olma fikri... onu tanımlayan biziz. Neyin adil olup neyin olmadığı benim ağzımdan çıkan iki kelimeyle belirlenir."
Kral bir adım yaklaştı. "Kardeşini asla haksız duruma düşürmeyeceksin. O da sana aynısını yapmayacak."

Baelenys'in elleri titriyordu. "Göğsündeki rozet öyle kafana göre çıkarıp takabileceğin bir oyuncak değil! 'İstediğin zaman geri al' diye bir şey yok! O rozeti taktığında tek bir kural vardır: Ben gel dediğimde gelirsin. Git dediğimde gidersin. Şu kararı ver dediğimde verirsin! Zaten oğlum olarak yapman gereken her şey!"
Baelor gergin bir şekilde boğazını temizledi. "Majesteleri, belki de dinlenmeliyiz."

Baelenys onu görmezden geldi, Jace'e o kadar yaklaştı ki Jace Kral'ın nefesindeki bayat şarabın kokusunu alabiliyordu. "Şimdi ortada bir dövüşerek yargılanma olduğuna göre... eğer bu Costayne, bu şövalye, her kimin sikindeyse, abine bir zarar verirse ne yapacaksın? Ya onu öldürürse? Adamı Duvar'a mahkum ettin. Eğer kazanırsa, onu tanrıların gözünde seçilmiş bir şampiyon yapmış olacaksın."
"Eğer bu adam gerçekten Gaelor'u öldürmeyi başarırsa," diye tükürdü Jace, "Krallığa bir iyilik yapmış olur!"
Baelenys donakaldı.
Baelor'a baktı. "Bu... bu siktiğimin..."

Baelenys Jace'e dönüp bakmadan devasa elini ileri fırlattı. Jace'i ceketinin yakasından yakalayıp öne doğru çekti ve elini Jace'in boğazına doladı. Yaşlı bir adamın dehşet verici gücüyle Kral, Jace'i aşağı doğru bastırdı ve oğlunun yüzünün yan tarafını ağır meşe masaya vahşice çarptı.
Baelor araya girmek için öne atıldı ama Baelenys boşta kalan eliyle onu itti.

"Kimin hakkında konuştuğunun farkında mısın?!" diye kükredi Baelenys, Jace'i masaya yapıştırırken dudaklarından tükürükler saçılıyordu. "O senin kardeşin! Tek bir kural var! Biriniz Kral olacak, diğeri de ne olursa olsun onu koruyacak, arkasını temizleyecek! Ve o adam sensin! Bu çocuğu varis ilan ettiğimde, başka kime güvenecek? Sırtını başka kime yaslayacak?!"
Şişmiş gözü acı verici bir şekilde meşeye bastırılmış olan Jace nefes almaya çalıştı. "Neden o olmak zorunda?!"
Baelenys tereddüt etti. Tutuşu gevşedi. Jace'in boynunu bıraktı ve geri çekildi.
Jace nefes nefese yavaşça doğrulurken, Baelenys yumruğunu düşen bir örs gücüyle masaya indirdi. Kalın meşe tam ortasından çatladı.
Kral arkasını döndü, balkona doğru yürüdü.
Baelor hızla Jace'i kontrol etti, gözleri sessiz bir soru soruyordu. Jace eliyle onu savuşturdu.
"Bunu duymamış olayım," dedi Baelenys ürkütücü derecede sessiz bir sesle. "Çık dışarı."

"Korkma, Baba," dedi Jace yakasını düzelterek. "Benim Demir Taht'ta gözüm yok. Ama en büyük çocuğun dışında birini varis ilan edebiliyorsan, neden bu yeteneksiz kas yığınını seçiyorsun? Merak etme, ben de bu aileye senin kadar bağlıyım. Sen kendin söyledin. Sana en çok benzeyenin ben olduğumu söyledin. İşte tam da bu yüzden bu hayvanı tahttan uzak tutmak bizim görevimiz. Onda ne görüyorsun? Seni iyi dinlemesini mi? Yirmi yıl boyunca barışı korudun. O adamın yönetimi altında iki yıl bile dayanamayız ve senin de bunun farkında olduğunu biliyorum. Bunu düşün."
Baelenys arkasını dönmedi. Baelor'la konuştu. "Çıkar şunu buradan, yoksa onu öldüreceğim."
Jace döndü ve güneş odasından çıktı. Koridor pencerelerinden, aşağıdaki bahçelerde yürüyen Alester ve Saera'yı bir anlığına gördü. Patlamış dudağından sızan kanı silen Jace, annesini bulmaya gitti.
Bit Çukuru'nun derinliklerinde Gaelor saatlerdir içiyordu.
Sör Saathos Maris, kırık kolu hala sıkıca bir askıya bağlı olarak karşısında oturuyordu. Meyhane gürültülü ve pis kokuluydu, prenslerin göz önünde saklanması için mükemmel bir yerdi.

"İnanılır gibi değil Prensim," diye mırıldandı Saathos, biradan dikkatli bir yudum alarak. "Görünüşe göre sizin için bu işten bir çıkış yolu yok. Prens sizi hedefi haline getirmiş. Size yardım etmek isterim ama haddimi aşmadan ne diyeceğimi bilemiyorum."
"O adam beni devirmek için elinden gelen her şeyi yapacak," dedi Gaelor kupasına dik dik bakarak.
"Sizi varis olarak tanımayı reddedeceğine inanıyor musunuz?"
"Elbette inanıyorum."

Saathos yapışkan masanın üzerinden daha da yaklaştı. "Eğer haddimi aşmıyorsam... bence de reddedecek. Ve inanıyorum ki Prens Jacaelon'un asıl motivasyonu sizin Demir Taht'a asla oturmamanızı garantilemek."

Gaelor içkisini dikti. "Ben Kral olduğumda, o adam beni öldürmek için ne gerekiyorsa yapacaktır. Diyarı bir iç savaşa sürüklemesinden korkuyorum. Babamın onlarca yıldır inşa ettiği barışı paramparça eden kral olarak hatırlanmak istemiyorum."
"Yani... sizce harekete mi geçmeliyiz?" diye sordu Saathos dikkatlice, nabız yoklayarak. "Söylemek istediğiniz bu mu, yoksa ben mi yanlış anlıyorum?"
Gaelor başını kaldırdı, mavi gözleri soğuk ve hesapçıydı.

"Siz son zamanlarda meşgul olduğunuz için, kaleye girip çıkarken birçok şey duydum," diye devam etti Saathos pürüzsüzce. "Ve inanıyorum ki düşüncelerinizde yalnız değilsiniz. Onunla doğrudan konuşmalısınız ama bence Üstat Cordin mevcut düzenin bozulmasını istemeyenlerden biri. O da... bizim gibi olabilir."
Gaelor yavaşça başını salladı. "Bir prens olarak görevim diyarda olabildiğince çok güç toplamaktır. Kral olduğumda, gerekirse onun da icabına bakılır."
İçmeye devam ettiler. Bu kez hesabı Saathos ödedi.
Jace Kraliçe Jaery'nin odasına doğru ilerlerken, bir oyuktan bir silüet çıktı.
Kral Eli'nin casusbaşı Weylar Rocke'tı.
"Prensim," diye fısıldadı Weylar. "Konuşmalıyız."
"Oldukça meşgulum," dedi Jace onu geçip giderek. "Ne var?"
"Bit Çukuru'ndaki son... karşılaşmanız hakkında," dedi Weylar hızla.
Jace olduğu yerde durdu. Koridora şöyle bir baktı. "Burada olmaz."
Jace'in özel çalışma odasına koştular. Jace kapıyı arkalarından kilitledi.
"Konuş," diye emretti Jace.

"Üstat Cordin ve Yüce Üstat Baelor'un o gece ne olduğunu ortaya çıkarmak için Bit Çukuru'nda burnunu sokan adamları var," diye rapor verdi Weylar. "Gerçeği öğrenip öğrenmediklerini henüz bilmiyorum. Ancak aramayı bölgenin dışına genişlettim. Günlerdir ortada yoktum çünkü şehri alt üst ettim."

Weylar sesini alçaltarak bir adım yaklaştı. "Tahmin edebileceğiniz gibi şüphelerimde haklıydım. Vahaemon'un Bit Çukuru'na yerleştirilmiş ajanları var. Fısıltılar, kör bir kadının bölge dışında birkaç kişiyle buluştuğunu söylüyor. Onları bulduk ve konuşturduk."
Jace kollarını kavuşturdu, şişmiş gözü zonkluyordu.
"Visenya buraya bir şey aramaya gelmiş," diye açıkladı Weylar. "Ve onun bir ejderha olduğuna inanıyorlar. O buraya bir ejderhayı evcilleştirmeye geldi."
Jace'in zihni hızla çalıştı. Visenya, Essos ve Volantis'teki kayıp metinleri tarıyordu. Dar Deniz'i geçtiyse, onların bilmediği bir şey biliyordu.

"Bildiğiniz gibi, ejderhalar hala güneyden göç ederek dönüyorlar," diye devam etti Weylar. "Sadece söylentilerle bilinen bir ejderhanın buralarda bulunabileceğine inanmış olmalı. Ancak bana sorarsanız... kendini size ifşa ettiğine göre, bu babası tarafından emredilmiş bir görev olmayabilir. Göz bağını çıkardığı an başarısız oldu. Ya da biz öyle düşünüyoruz."
"İyi iş, Weylar," dedi Jace, ağır bir altın kesesini masanın üzerine fırlatarak.
Weylar altını yakalayarak gülümsedi. "Ah, Prensim, hiç gerek yoktu. Sizinle bizim farklı bir hukukumuz var. Beni yanınıza daha çok alırsanız..."
Jace, makam atlamaya yönelik bu bariz girişimi görmezden geldi. "Bu ejderha da ne? Elimizde ekstra bir bilgi var mı? Visenya'nın nereye kaybolduğunu gören var mı? Herhangi bir tahmin?"

"On yıllardır burada yaşayan yaşlı bir adamı köşeye sıkıştırdık," dedi Weylar, ses tonu ciddileşerek. "Westeros'lu olduğu için özel bir bilgisi yoktu ama Essos'luların bir isim fısıldadığını duymuş. Hayalet ejderhanın soyundan geldiğini söylediler."
Yamyam. Ya da onun soyundan doğmuş bir şey.
"Anlaşıldı," dedi Jace. "Başka bir şey var mı? Bir sonraki hamlen ne?"
"Başka bir şey yok Prensim. Daha ne olsun?" Weylar gergin bir şekilde kıkırdadı. "Doğrusu... Bence bu çok muazzam bir keşif."
"Pekala. Altınını almadın mı?" diye sordu Jace manalı bir şekilde.
Weylar gergin bir gülümseme sundu, başını eğdi ve odadan sıvıştı.

title: Chapter XIV: The Reunion
synopsis: As the Crown attempts to settle a brewing war in the Riverlands, an uncomfortable family reunion on Dragonstone brings old grievances to light.
content: The days following the trial of Ser Brant Costayne passed like sand slipping through an hourglass, steady and quiet, yet carrying the undeniable weight of impending change. Within the red walls of the capital, the Targaryen siblings fell into their respective rhythms.

Gaelor sought solace where he often did, in the arms of his wife. With Naella's pregnancy officially known to the court, the Crown Prince seemed to mellow, retreating into the private chambers they shared. Jacaelon, meanwhile, busied himself with two very different pursuits. The first was the education of little Princess Vhaemys, a task he found surprisingly pleasant, despite the girl's persistent habit of treating her lessons as a mummer's farce. The second pursuit occupied his evenings, spent in the company of Lady Lorenah Dayne.

Jace had begun training his young dragon, Jhagar, with a very specific maneuver in mind—one involving a carefully crafted necklace. It was a tedious process, but Jace was nothing if not patient when he wanted something.
The Second Day of the Eighth Moon, Ninety-Nine AC

Two days had passed since the uproar in the Great Hall. Jace sat in the Hand's chair, the heavy wood pressing against his aching back. The morning had been a steady stream of merchants complaining of tariffs and minor lords squabbling over fishing rights. Now, the final audience of the day stood before him, and the air in the throne room felt instantly heavier.
Lord Godfrey Blackwood marched toward the dais, his boots ringing sharply against the stone. He did not bow; he merely stopped and glared up at the Hand.
"I have a matter to bring before the Crown," Godfrey announced, his voice tight with suppressed rage.
Jace leaned forward, resting his chin on his steepled fingers. "Speak, Lord Blackwood."

"You know well that House Blackwood and House Bracken have watered the Riverlands with each other's blood for centuries," Godfrey began. "We have held a brittle peace of late. Yet, Lord Perric Bracken has chosen to break it. Willingly."

Jace kept his face impassive. The Blackwoods and the Brackens were a headache older than the Iron Throne itself. Lord Clover Tully, the Lord Paramount of the Trident, was notoriously passive, a man who preferred diplomacy to steel, often leaving his unruly bannermen to their own devices.

"A few days ago," Godfrey continued, his voice rising, "my cousins and their sworn swords were celebrating near the Bracken border. They had drunk deeply. The Brackens claim they crossed the boundary line. For this 'trespass', Bracken men slaughtered my cousin in cold blood."

Godfrey sneered, his hands clenching into fists. "Lord Perric had the audacity to declare that his men were merely issuing a warning, and that my cousin's death was an unfortunate accident during the altercation. This was no accident. It was a deliberate provocation. I have come to seek the Crown's leave. I intend to declare war on House Bracken, and I will not stop until their lands burn. Either I do this, or the Crown must take immediate action against them."

Jace exchanged a brief look with his uncle Baelor, who stood nearby. "My lord," Jace said smoothly, "before bringing this before the Crown, have you sought the judgment of your liege lord, Clover Tully?"
"Of course I did," Godfrey spat. "But I did not receive the answer I required."
Jace knew exactly why. Only a few moons prior, one of Lord Tully's grandsons had wed a Bracken girl.
"What answer did you expect, and what did you receive?" Jace asked.

"I expected permission for vengeance, or for him to marshal his own forces to punish them. Instead, Lord Tully insisted it was a drunken mistake and that we must not end years of peace over it. So, I came to you. I told Lord Tully as much. I told him if he would not give me justice, I would find it in the Red Keep."

Jace sighed inwardly. "Lord Blackwood, based on your own account, the Crown cannot ascertain the true intent behind this skirmish. It is entirely possible it was, in fact, a tragic mistake born of drunken folly. If you were to march on Stone Hedge now, claiming the Crown's blessing... with all due respect to the ancient history of your houses, you would transform a border dispute into a crisis that could engulf the entire realm. What exactly do you expect from us?"

Godfrey’s jaw tightened. "I expect justice. And if I do not find it here..." He turned his head slightly, addressing the gallery as much as the Hand. "...then, much like our Lord Tully building ties with the Brackens, perhaps House Blackwood should ride North and speak with Lord Rickard Stark."
Jace did not flinch, but his eyes narrowed. A thinly veiled threat to draw the North into Riverlands politics. He leaned back and murmured to Baelor, "Thoughts, Uncle?"

"It was done on purpose, without a doubt," Baelor whispered back, adjusting his chain. "It is always the same with them. Even in times of absolute peace, a Blackwood will find a reason to kill a Bracken, and vice versa. You cannot trust either of them in this. They bring their petty feuds to our doorstep, creating problems where none need exist. Perhaps we should summon Lord Tully."
"Tully is tied to the Brackens now," Jace murmured. "What good will his word do?"
Baelor offered a faint, dry smile. "Then, as Hand and Prince, the matter rests with you."

Jace straightened, his gaze turning hard as he looked back at Godfrey. "The Crown will have no part in this conflict, Lord Blackwood. To resolve this matter with the least bloodshed, I offer you two paths. The first: we will dispatch an envoy to investigate and report back to the Crown. You will wait patiently for our decision. The second: you and Lord Bracken will resolve this matter between yourselves, man to man, in a trial by combat. If Lord Bracken refuses the challenge, the Crown will reconsider its stance."

Godfrey considered this for a long moment, the anger in his eyes settling into a cold determination. "Very well, Lord Hand. I shall send a raven to Stone Hedge immediately. I assume the envoy will be sent from the Red Keep?"
"Of course."
Godfrey bowed stiffly and departed.
Jace glanced at his mother and Baelor in the gallery. Both offered subtle nods of approval. Jace let out a long breath, suddenly feeling exhausted. The court was dismissed.
That evening, the royal family dined together in a rare display of unity. It had been moons since they had all shared a table.

King Baelenys sat at the head, tearing at a roasted capon. Queen Jaery sat to his right, Gaelor to his left. Down the long table sat Maela, Saera, Naella, Baelor, little Vhaemys, and Jace, who occupied the seat directly opposite the King.
The conversation flowed easily enough, mostly centered on trivial matters.
"We must attend the feast tomorrow," Jaery remarked, placing a hand gently on Baelenys's arm.
The King paused, chewing slowly, and let out a heavy sigh.
Saera leaned close to Jace. "Tomorrow is Uncle Malaenar's nameday," she whispered.

Baelenys stopped eating, turning his fork lazily in his hand. He looked down the table at his children. "They are busy," the King said gruffly. "Jace has the court to run. People to listen to." He glanced sideways at Gaelor. "And I am sure this one has something to do as well."
"I would like to go," Gaelor said immediately.
Baelenys shot him a sharp look, then turned his gaze to Jace. "Are you not too busy tomorrow?"
"I have duties every day, Father," Jace replied evenly.
"Exactly," Baelenys grumbled. "And it would hardly be proper to leave one of you behind while the rest of us go."
"Let us all go," Jaery urged gently. "It will be a change of scenery. We will be together."
Jace nodded. "My work can be delayed for a day. It is not an issue. Let us go together."
Baelor spoke up from his cup of wine. "I shall remain in the capital. I can oversee the Crown's affairs in the Hand's absence."
"Very well," Baelenys said, tossing his fork onto his plate. "Suddenly everyone wishes to be a family. Fine. We go tomorrow. We will visit him."
The matter settled, Jace turned his attention to Saera. "You have been scarce lately. What occupies your time?"
"Vhaemys," Saera said, reaching out to pat the little girl's head. "I have been looking after her."
Jace raised an eyebrow. "Have you? Because I have also been spending time with Vhaemys."

"Then perhaps you could spend some time with her at night," Saera said, lowering her voice so the King would not hear. "She has been having trouble sleeping. Terrible nightmares. She wakes up terrified."
"Have you told Mother?" Jace asked, concerned.

"I told her Vhaemys wasn't sleeping well, but not the contents of the dreams," Saera murmured. "Mother is already suffocating under the weight of dealing with Father... and with you all. I didn't want to add to her burdens."
"What is she dreaming about?"
"Dragons," Saera whispered. "A massive, white dragon."
Jace felt a chill run down his spine. He remembered Baelor's old texts about Dreamers. "I will look into it," he promised quietly.
"Please do," Saera sighed. "It is exhausting. She wants to be with me, but she also asks for you constantly."
"As you know, I have taken over her education," Jace said, leaning closer so only Saera could hear. "Because if left to her own devices, this girl will turn out exactly like our father."

The dinner concluded without further incident. Later, out on the balconies, Jace and Saera stood looking out over the city. Vhaemys had already been put to bed. Gaelor lounged in the shadows down the corridor, idly watching them.
Ser Alester Dayne emerged from the darkness, a sealed piece of parchment in his hand. He walked directly to Saera.
"Princess, a raven arrived for you," Alester said, holding out the letter.
"Ah, thank you," Saera said, breaking the wax seal.
As she read, her eyes narrowed slightly, trying to make out the words in the dim light. A slow, undeniable blush crept up her cheeks. She smiled, a genuine, unguarded expression.
Alester watched her, a knot forming in his stomach.

The letter was from the North. It was a simple message from Rickard Stark: *"I would wholeheartedly desire Princess Saera Targaryen to visit the North once more. Your previous visit was sudden, and we would wish to host you far better this time."*
Saera chuckled softly to herself, folding the parchment.

Maela, who had just stepped onto the balcony, snatched the letter from Saera's hand before she could stop her. She began to read it aloud, a teasing lilt in her voice. Saera quickly snatched it back, glaring at her sister.
Alester stood frozen, his face a mask of shock. He looked at Jace, a silent plea for an explanation in his eyes.
"What is this about?" Jace asked, looking between Saera and the knight.
"I don't know," Saera said, still smiling.
Gaelor called out from the corridor, "I haven't seen you this happy in a long time, Saera."
"Were you standing there this whole time?" Saera retorted.
Alester looked around nervously, his heart hammering against his ribs.
Saera, more amused by her siblings' reactions than annoyed, laughed. "I am going to my chambers. If there is nothing else."
She pushed past them.
Gaelor sneered at Maela. "You should go too, Maela. Maybe you'll find yourself a Northern knight."
Maela wrinkled her nose in disgust. "Are you finding many in the brothels these days?"
"What business would I have in a brothel?" Gaelor shot back indignantly. "I am a married man."
Jace coughed pointedly.
Maela sneered mockingly. "They say half the brats in Flea Bottom have silver hair now."
As Alester hurried to follow Saera, he accidentally bumped hard into Jace's shoulder. He didn't even notice, his eyes fixed on the Princess.
"Princess," Alester called out as he caught up to her.
Saera kept walking, though she slowed her pace.
"Are you... going to Winterfell then?" Alester asked, his voice tight.
Before she could answer, he added hastily, "But weren't you coming to Dragonstone tomorrow?"
"Of course I am," Saera said. "I suppose I'll go to Winterfell some time after that."
They stepped out of the shadows, the moonlight washing over their faces. A long silence stretched between them. Alester looked desperately around the empty corridor, struggling to find the words.
"But then..." he started, stopping again. He took a deep breath. "Then we will have to pause our walks."
Saera let out a soft sigh. "We were only going to walk up to a point, Alester. We weren't going to keep walking until I turned fifty."

She saw the pain in his eyes and her expression softened. "You are one of the people I value most in this entire castle. I have no intention of changing that. But at the end of the day, I am a princess."
Alester nodded slowly, the words landing like stones.
Jace caught up to them just as Saera turned toward her door.
"What is going on here? Is there a problem?" Jace demanded, looking at his sworn sword.
"The man she saw exactly once is Lord Rickard Stark," Alester muttered, sounding thoroughly defeated. "I don't understand why she is so eager."
"You need to do something," Jace told him.
Alester looked down at himself, defeated. "If it were you, maybe. What can I do? What could I possibly say?" He paused. "Besides, the King would never allow it."
"Are you a fool?" Jace snapped. "Who cares about the King or the Lord? You are going to do something. Don't look for excuses. Stop being a coward."
"What do you want me to do? Go into her room right now?" Alester asked, exasperated.
"Yes, go. Tell her exactly how you feel. You will regret it if you don't," Jace commanded.
Alester turned and walked toward Saera's door. He raised his fist to knock.
From inside, he heard voices. Queen Jaery had joined Saera.
Saera was speaking animatedly about the beauty of Winterfell, describing it as the most breathtaking place she had ever seen. Jaery's voice was equally excited.
"Four years ago," Jaery was saying, "Brandon Stark and Rickard Stark attended a feast at Riverrun." She paused. "I wonder how your father will react."
Saera did not respond immediately.
"He is a very handsome lord, truly," Jaery added.
"I thought so too," Saera replied. "Well, from what I could see."
Soft laughter echoed from the room.
Alester lowered his hand. The words he had meant to say died in his throat. He turned and walked away, the crushing weight of reality settling heavily upon his shoulders.
The Fourth Day of the Eighth Moon, Ninety-Nine AC

The Targaryen royal family arrived on Dragonstone. Jace had invited Lorenah to accompany them. King Baelenys paid her presence no mind, though Queen Jaery seemed pleased enough. Little Vhaemys, however, remained distant and openly sullen.
"Have you ever even seen the sea before?" Vhaemys asked Lorenah bluntly as they walked the dark stone corridors. "What is a desert rat doing near a dragon?"
It was a clumsy, insulting attempt at hostility, but Lorenah merely laughed it off, completely unbothered.
Jace flushed with embarrassment. "Vhaemys, do not say such things," he hissed, pulling the girl aside.
Vhaemys crossed her arms, glaring up at him. "See what a good father you have? He never scolds you like that."
Further ahead, Naella leaned close to Gaelor. "Do you think we will be moving to Dragonstone? Will we live here soon?"
"Only if I am named heir soon," Gaelor replied casually. "Otherwise, there will be blood in the Red Keep anyway. Though it might be boring here."
Naella smirked, teasing him with her old suspicions. "Why? Because there are no brothels?"
"No," Gaelor laughed, missing the barb entirely. "Because I wouldn't be able to spend time with Saathos."

Dragonstone was a fortress of dark wonder, carved from the living rock of a volcanic island. Great stone gargoyles in the shape of dragons snarled from the battlements, and the very air smelled of sulfur and salt. It was a harsh, unforgiving place, beautiful only to those who held the blood of Old Valyria.
The evening feast was a surprisingly modest affair. The great hall was lit only by flickering candles. There were no other invited guests, no grand preparations.

At one end of the massive feasting table sat Prince Malaenar. Beside him sat a seventeen-year-old girl, undeniably beautiful, but with the unmistakable, rough-hewn features of the lowborn. This was Tansy. She had ensnared Malaenar two years prior, a fact the royal family deeply resented. It was evident to anyone with eyes that the girl was digging for gold. It was equally evident that she had organized this entire gathering without Malaenar's prior knowledge.
Malaenar looked at Baelenys, a playful, drunken smirk on his face. "...so it goes. Who knows how you would have reacted if you were me. But she made a little surprise for me."
Gaelor leaned over and whispered to Saera, "Who the fuck is she to summon the royal family?"
Saera, though she agreed, nudged him sharply with her elbow to stay quiet.
Baelenys and Malaenar were not close, but they had been drinking heavily together for the past hour in relative silence. Baelenys did not react to Malaenar's comment.

Malaenar sighed heavily, turning his gaze to Jaery. "I wish I could stand, so I will have to do it like this." He raised his goblet. "I drink to our family. It is a wonderful, and surprising, feeling to see my brother and his family here after so long. Whether it is my nameday or not. It seems our King has decided to be a brother again." He swayed slightly, heavily intoxicated. "Welcome back."
The table remained dead silent.
"It was very kind of you to arrange this," Jaery said diplomatically, breaking the tension. "We were quite surprised, truthfully."
Baelenys grunted, swirling the wine in his cup. "We haven't exactly been invited often. Not that we desired it, but the invitations were lacking."

Malaenar scoffed softly. "Truthfully, a feast could have been held here on Dragonstone for your child. After all, if you are to be the heir, your child will one day be King." His words were slurred, his gaze drifting toward Gaelor.
"Our father will decide that," Gaelor said flatly.

The heavy doors of the hall swung open. A man stepped inside, ducking slightly to clear the frame. He was nearly seven feet tall, a mountain of muscle wrapped in simple plate. He carried a greatsword strapped to his back.
Everyone recognized him.

Baran Strong. The knight who had been expelled from the Kingsguard alongside Curtass Whent. The two had brawled viciously within the Red Keep. While both had been stripped of their white cloaks, Baran had been deemed the party in the right, and was exiled to serve as a sworn sword on Dragonstone.
He moved silently through the room, spoke briefly with a servant, and turned to leave.

"I might have sent you one of the finest knights in the Seven Kingdoms, just so you know," Malaenar slurred, gesturing vaguely toward Baran. "The kind of man you'd want in the Red Keep." He chuckled. "But I'm not giving him back. Consider him a gift from a brother."
Baelenys remained silent, his jaw clenched, looking utterly exhausted by the evening.
Jace leaned close to Lorenah, whispering under his breath. "I am so suffocated. I wish we could just leave. We could have been having dinner with Alester right now."
"If you'll excuse us," Jace announced, standing up and offering his arm to Lorenah. "We require some fresh air." He gestured for Vhaemys to follow.
As they stood, Baelenys finally spoke, his voice cutting through the hall, returning to the very beginning of the conversation.
"Have you truly acted as an elder brother to me, up to this point?"
Malaenar let out a sharp, bitter bark of laughter. "Hah. Same old song. Always the same song."
"Did you act as my brother when Vahaemon was stabbing me in the back?" Baelenys demanded, his voice rising. "Did you help me when our father was doing those things to our mother?"
"You were the one closest to Father!" Malaenar fired back. "You only tried to stop things years later. And besides, I renounced the throne! How much more of a brother am I supposed to be?"
"Exactly," Baelenys sneered. "You stepped aside so two brothers could kill each other, and you washed your hands of everything."
Jaery quickly intervened, desperately trying to steer the conversation back to safer, mundane topics.

"What was I supposed to do?" Malaenar demanded, ignoring her. "Spend my life recounting your glories? Should we sing of the Iron Islands tonight?" He looked at Gaelor. "Who knows how many times you've heard the tale of 'The Dragon's Breath against Harrik the Drowned Servant'."
Tansy, sensing the escalating danger, placed a hand on Malaenar's arm. "Let us not speak of such things on such a beautiful evening, with our family gathered and our King present."
Malaenar placed his hand over hers, holding Baelenys's gaze in a silent challenge.

Tansy turned to the King. "My King," she said smoothly, then looked at Gaelor. "I am so deeply honored that you graced us with your presence today. Especially knowing that the two most important figures of House Targaryen are currently sitting at our table."
Gaelor drained the last of his wine, smiled pleasantly, and held out his cup to a passing maid. "Would you refill this?"
Tansy, realizing she had been completely ignored, faltered. "Well, anyway..."
As Gaelor reached for the refilled cup, Baelenys snatched it from the maid's hand and hurled it across the table. It shattered against the stone floor directly in front of Malaenar and Tansy.
Both of them froze.
"You heard your prince," Baelenys growled at Tansy.
He then turned his blazing eye upon his crippled brother. "Tell your wench to pour some wine."
Maela gasped, covering her mouth with her hands, exchanging a horrified look with Jaery.
Malaenar slammed his hands onto the table, his face purpling with rage.
The King stood up, his massive frame dominating the room. "What are you going to do?" he mocked. "Are you not going to stand your ground?"
The two brothers began screaming at one another.

"This is why I am the way I am!" Baelenys roared over the din. "You all see me as tense and angry, well this is why! Look at this family!" He pointed at Saera and Maela. "These are my daughters." He pointed at Malaenar. "One brother is a traitor, and the other is this fucking cripple! My sons are trying to slit each other's throats..."
The argument devolved into pure chaos.
Gaelor stood up slowly. "Thanks for the feast, Uncle," he said calmly, and walked out of the hall.
He descended into the cool night air of the courtyard, the sounds of his father and uncle still echoing from the open windows above.
"My father went a little far," Gaelor remarked to Naella, who had followed him.
"But what your uncle did was no better," Naella countered. "Bringing some unknown girl into Dragonstone and putting her at the high table."
"Don't ask," Gaelor muttered.
He spotted Saathos, Baran Strong, and Alester drinking near the stables. He walked over to join them.
"How fares the Red Keep?" Baran asked as Gaelor approached.
"I am having the time of my life," Saathos replied sarcastically, taking a swig of wine.
"I heard Curtass Whent is dead," Baran noted casually.
"So they say," Alester replied, his face an impassive mask as he took a sip from his own cup. "The life of a knight, I suppose."
"I don't know many knights capable of facing Curtass Whent," Gaelor mused, his eyes tracking the shadows.

Baran spat onto the dirt. "Curtass Whent was no true knight. I could kill a man like that any day of the week. Curtass was nothing special." He looked directly at Gaelor. "My prince, when you spend your life on Dragonstone, you begin to miss the action. We bow to the King's commands, of course, but it burns a man to be exiled here because of a piece of shit like Curtass Whent, especially when he was in the right."
Saathos grinned. "Then Prince Gaelor should bring you to the Red Keep."
Baran's eyes lit up with sudden hope.
"Is it your place to decide that?" Gaelor snapped at Saathos.
Saathos immediately bowed his head. "No, my prince. Forgive me."
"How good is he?" Gaelor asked, looking Baran up and down.
"No, my prince, I only meant... I know how much you enjoy sparring with strong knights," Saathos amended quickly.
Baran steered the conversation back to safer waters. "So, my prince, who killed Curtass Whent then? I despised the man, but he was Kingsguard once, even if he was a cunt."
"I never liked him from the moment I laid eyes on him," Gaelor said, leaning against a post. "But I don't know. As I said, a large, blonde knight supposedly killed him. Saathos heard the reports."
Alester cast a quick, sideways glance at Saathos. He had no idea such an investigation had taken place.
"I must say," Baran continued, looking pointedly at Alester, "the image of the Kingsguard has certainly changed. They seem to prefer pretty faces these days."
"I suppose that is the Kingsguard's greatest flaw these days," Alester replied mildly, refusing to take the bait.
Gaelor turned back to Baran. "If you're willing to risk it, we will speak to my uncle Malaenar. Come with me to the capital."
"Truly?" Baran asked, stunned. "Would they permit it?"
"If I ask, they will permit it. If they wish, we will send a knight from the Red Keep to replace you."
"I would rather spend my days in the Red Keep with you than another day here," Baran said earnestly.
"It is a good place," Saathos agreed.
Baran looked at Saathos's sling. "How did you break your arm? On one of your adventures with the Prince?"
Saathos bristled slightly. "Something like that."
"Prince Jacaelon broke it," Alester supplied helpfully.
"Did he?" Baran looked impressed, turning to Gaelor. "Wait, in the tourney? The battle between the princes was heard in every corner of the realm. They will speak of it for a long time."
Gaelor snorted. "Tell me about it."
On a balcony just above the courtyard, Jace, Lorenah, and Vhaemys were talking. Saera soon joined them.
Jace had lifted Vhaemys and set her upon the wide stone balustrade. The little girl was excitedly recounting her dream.
"...and then... and then I saw this huge white dragon..." she chattered happily.
Saera looked over the edge of the balcony, her eyes finding the group of knights below. For a fleeting second, she locked eyes with Alester. He immediately looked away.
Lorenah stood beside Saera as the muffled sounds of shouting from the Great Hall finally began to die down.
"You seem to enjoy the view," Lorenah observed quietly.
"What do you mean?" Saera asked.
"I've noticed it in the Red Keep as well," Lorenah said, a knowing smile on her lips. "You seem to enjoy spending time with Ser Alester."
"He is like family to us," Saera replied defensively. "Especially to Jace and me."
Jace, half-listening, chimed in. "He's like a brother to me, yes, but I haven't quite figured out what he is to you."
Vhaemys swung her legs, listening intently to the adults.
"He is as close as a knight can be to a princess," Saera said firmly.
"Why? Do Targaryen princesses have such strict boundaries?" Jace teased.
"Let's stop talking about me and talk about you two," Saera deflected.
Lorenah stepped closer to Jace, her arm brushing against his. "I am merely a Dornish girl our prince enjoys spending time with before he sends her home," she purred.
Vhaemys immediately spoke up, her face scrunched in a scowl. "Good. Know your place."
Lorenah burst into genuine, delighted laughter.

Saera reached out and pinched Vhaemys's ear hard. The little girl yelped in pain, tears springing to her eyes. "I'm going to tell Father on you!" she cried, scrambling off the balustrade and running inside.
"You hurt her," Lorenah noted.
"She'll live," Saera said dismissively. "She needs to learn her place."
A cold sea breeze swept over the balcony. Lorenah shivered, rubbing her arms. Jace unclasped his heavy cloak and draped it over her shoulders.
"How romantic," Saera mocked dryly. She turned to Jace. "We are going to talk later. You won't escape so easily." She turned and followed Vhaemys inside.
Jace and Lorenah were left alone in the moonlight.
"What are we doing? Where do we stand in all this?" Lorenah asked, gesturing vaguely toward the hall where the King had been screaming moments before.
She looked back out at the sea. "So... is Prince Gaelor destined to spend his life here, waiting until he takes the throne?"
Jace let out a sharp bark of laughter. "HAH! You actually think he's going to sit on the throne?"
Lorenah paused, studying his face. "What exactly is the root of this hatred between you two? I know of the recent events, but there must be a history. How can brothers be like this?"
"Exactly as you've seen him act recently," Jace said, his voice hard. "That meathead has been exactly like that since we were children."
"But the King does not seem pleased with the situation either," she noted.

"What is there for the King to be pleased about, aside from Gaelor's sycophancy?" Jace countered bitterly. "Look at me. Despite my lack of experience, I am doing everything in my power to hold this realm together, and you see the treatment I receive."
Lorenah leaned back against the balustrade, arching her spine slightly as she looked up at him. "What will happen to Prince Visenor?"
"I have no idea," Jace admitted. "I must thank you again for everything you have done. I need to speak with him directly soon."
"A raven arrived the other day," Lorenah said softly. "Do not worry, it was sent securely. Your brother is expecting a child."
Jace blinked, genuinely shocked. "Do you know how long she has been with child?"
"The raven arrived recently, so she must be roughly three moons along," Lorenah estimated.
"I need to find out the truth of this," Jace muttered, running a hand through his hair. "Things could become far more complicated than they already are."

"There is something else," Lorenah added hesitantly. "Prince Visenor left for a short journey and has not returned for some time. Princess Rhaella is reportedly very anxious, especially given her condition."
"That is all we needed," Jace sighed heavily. "I will have to go there as soon as possible and find out what is happening. Thank you."
"It might be best if I returned home soon, before I get caught in the middle of this chaos," Lorenah said carefully. "The same letter mentioned that my father expects my return."
Panic flared briefly in Jace's chest. "Wait, where are you going? I haven't even been able to properly host you since you arrived."
He stepped closer. "Besides, I haven't given you my surprise yet."
Lorenah smiled, intrigued. "What kind of surprise? Is it something you can give me here?"
"No," Jace said, his eyes darkening slightly. "You will find out when we return to the Red Keep."
Lorenah laughed, a bright sound that carried over the waves.
On another balcony overlooking the sea, Malaenar and Baelenys stood side-by-side, drinking wine in relative calm.
"You shouldn't give that nobody so much influence," Baelenys said quietly, referring to Tansy. "I don't want my children or my family seeing such things."
"There is only so much a man can do on Dragonstone," Malaenar replied.
"You isolated yourself here," Baelenys pointed out.
"Why?" Malaenar scoffed. "Does the whole family yearn to see me in the Red Keep?"

"Are you not doing the exact same thing?" Malaenar challenged.

"Because mine is the truth. Because I am right. I stood against our brother, against our mother, and when necessary, against our father. And you all gathered together, spun a tale, and painted me as an unbearable, bitter old man for doing what had to be done."
Malaenar chuckled softly. "You are."
Baelenys didn't look at him. "Fuck off."
They stood in silence for a long time.
"Even though I never showed it," Malaenar said finally, his voice stripping away years of resentment, "I always envied you. Especially for how you stood up to our father."
Baelenys looked surprised. "Our father lost his mind as he aged."
"He was a vile man," Malaenar said.

Taking advantage of Baelenys's silence, Malaenar continued. "You saw the bruises on our mother's arms and back more than anyone. Yet you still won't say it. You won't admit that our father was a useless, dishonorable bastard."
Baelenys maintained his silence, staring out at the dark water.
Finally, he turned to his elder brother. "He is dead and gone. There is no need to speak of it anymore. We must never speak ill of our family. Not to the outside world."
And so, the two old men continued to drink.
A maester hurried across the courtyard, carrying a sealed letter.
Gaelor intercepted him. He snatched the letter from the maester's hands and broke the seal.
It was from Baelor Targaryen.

"We accomplished what we set out to do regarding Pentos. Vahaemon and his convoy were denied entry to the city. They have set sail for Tyrosh. However, according to an informant within his camp, Vahaemon intends to offer Tyrosh the protection of his dragon in exchange for sanctuary and support."

While it was a diplomatic triumph for Jace and Baelor, Gaelor saw only an opportunity. A chance for military glory. A chance to strike two birds with one stone: secure the Stepstones and eliminate Vahaemon. Gaelor's blood pounded with excitement.
He hurried to find his father.
He passed Tansy in the hall. He let his gaze linger on her, openly admiring her form. She noticed, holding his gaze for a second too long, before Gaelor continued on his way.
He found King Baelenys and Malaenar speaking normally, as if they hadn't been at each other's throats an hour before. Gaelor accepted it as standard Targaryen behavior.
"A letter from Uncle Baelor, Father," Gaelor said, handing over the parchment.
Baelenys read it without displaying much emotion, though his shoulders seemed to relax slightly. He looked around, searching for the wine pitcher.
Malaenar noticed. "Pour your prince some wine," he commanded.
"No, I shall take my leave," Gaelor said.
"Go to your wife," the King ordered.
As Gaelor turned to leave, the maids were clearing the tables in the adjoining room. Tansy approached him, holding out a goblet. "You asked for wine, my prince."
Gaelor took the goblet, downed the wine in a single long swallow, and shoved the empty cup back into her hands.
He walked away quickly, his blood running hot, knowing that if he stayed a moment longer in his current state of arousal, he would do something he might regret.
He went straight to Naella's chambers to relieve his tension.
Jace found Vhaemys in her bedchamber, preparing for sleep.
"Did your sister leave?" Jace asked.
"Yes. She apologized," Vhaemys said haughtily. She glared at her maid. "Get out."
The maid bowed her head and scrambled from the room.
"Did you forgive her?" Jace asked, sitting on the edge of the bed.
"I will think about it until morning."

"We cannot treat our guests this way, Vhaemys. You pushed your luck," Jace chided gently. "Even if you don't like her, Lorenah likes you. She just laughed it off. Saera apologized too. Be the bigger person, accept the apology, and make peace."

"That is not true," Jace said. "Look, I took over your education without anyone asking me to. Don't be unfair."
"Fine," Vhaemys huffed. "But when is she leaving? Doesn't she have a home?"
"I have a surprise for both of you first," Jace said, his eyes glinting with secret amusement. "But to find out what it is, you must behave, and you must go to sleep right now."
Vhaemys’s eyes lit up. "Alright!"
"Do I have your word?"
